summary: This Dockerfile builds a Ubuntu container with the xmlstarlet tool installed for XML processing. It creates a demo directory with a sample XML file of book data, customizes the shell prompt to show a whale emoji and username, then starts an interactive bash shell when the container runs.

explanations.3: This tells Ubuntu's package manager to skip interactive prompts during installation, so the build doesn't hang waiting for user input.
explanations.5: The && chains commands together so they all run as one step—this keeps the Docker layer count down and makes the build more efficient.
explanations.8: After installing packages, we delete the package manager cache to shrink the final image size, since we won't need to install anything else.
explanations.11: mkdir -p creates the /root/demo directory; the -p flag means 'create parent directories if needed and don't error if it already exists'.
explanations.12: printf '%s' outputs the XML string exactly as-is without adding a newline at the end, then > redirects it into the data.xml file.
explanations.18: This appends a fancy bash prompt configuration to the user's .bashrc file so every new shell session shows a whale emoji and the current username.
explanations.20: The -i flag runs bash in interactive mode, which means you can type commands when you enter the container instead of it just exiting.
